claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.note: Heading at the wrong level: the transcription's convention is one '#' per numbering component (7. is '#', 7.1 '##', 6.4.1 '###', 6.4.2.1 '####', 6.4.2.1.1 '#####'); should be '####' like 6.4.2.1.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page IV-39 (PDF p185) shows the heading '6.4.2.3 Imperative Statements and Imperative Sentences', a four-component number. The markdown (specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 7701) renders it '### ', the same level as its parent '### 6.4.2 Statements and Sentences' (line 7623), while its sibling '#### 6.4.2.1 Conditional Statements and Sentences' (line 7629) is at '####' and 6.4.2.1.1 at '#####'. So the heading is present but one level too shallow, breaking the outline. The same page's children inherit the error: '#### 6.4.2.3.1' and '#### 6.4.2.3.2' should be '#####', and '### 6.4.2.4 Delimited Scope Statements' should be '####' (and the preceding page's '### 6.4.2.2' likewise).
verdict.corrected_description: Heading is not missing but at the wrong level: '### 6.4.2.3' should be '#### 6.4.2.3' (sibling of '#### 6.4.2.1'); on the same page '#### 6.4.2.3.1' and '#### 6.4.2.3.2' should be '#####', and '### 6.4.2.4' should be '####'.
